messages:
maria-ops: noticed a sharp P99 spike for na-east runtime starting ~1998765400, impact on small latency-sensitive routes. saw GPU pool reporting reduced capacity + control-plane errors. anyone else?
jamal-infra: yep, seeing control-plane heartbeats delayed to some hosts, worker registry shows some nodes flapping out then back in. network telemetry shows increased retransmits to the na-east NAT cluster.
lisa-sre: alerting graph: p50 flat, p95 slight, p99 doubled. errors are 504-ish timeouts coming from runtime->batcher RPCs.
kevin-runtime: digging into runtime logs — continuous-batcher is building huge aggregate batches intermittently when a subset of backends go quiet, KV cache miss rate spikes. looks like batching windows inflate when a node drops then returns.
maria-ops: that fits: control-plane flaps make the router think capacity dropped so it tries to consolidate into fewer workers and batch size grows, but those workers then get saturated -> tail latency.
ops-bot: Incident: svc=runtime-na-east severity=high triggered at 1998765428 (auto). Incident channel created: #incident-1998765432.
jamal-infra: immediate mitigation plan: 1) limit continuous-batcher max_batch_size to 32 2) disable aggressive prefix coalescing 3) route 10% traffic to na-west fallback pool 4) mark suspect hosts as draining so router avoids them. can someone run ramps?
kevin-runtime: applying hotpatch to batcher config now: `kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/batcher MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 CONTINUOUS_BATCHER_ENABLED=false` — rolling restart.
lisa-sre: I'm initiating traffic shift: `routingctl shift --from na-east --to na-west --percent 10 --reason "batcher mitigation"` — starting at 1998765440. watching for error increase.
maria-ops: ops-infra, can we mark those 3 hosts (na-east-rt-07..09) draining? they show repeated heartbeat misses.
jamal-infra: marking as draining now. `hostsctl set-state na-east-rt-07,na-east-rt-08,na-east-rt-09 draining` — should prevent new allocations.
kevin-runtime: also bumped kvcache eviction aggressiveness to avoid large KV growth during intermittent reconnects: `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6` set on runtime.
lisa-sre: after shift + config changes, p99 dropped ~35% in the last 90s. small success. errors trend down.
maria-ops: good. next steps: keep 10% diverted for 15m, if stable reduce to 5% then restore. open ticket to upstream networking to investigate NAT cluster retransmits.
jamal-infra: +1. we should also add routing guard: if control-plane reports >3 host flaps in 60s, temporarily cap max_batch_size to 16 for 5m. can file a quick PR.
kevin-runtime: created PR #3421 with safeguard + unit tests, marking for urgent review. linking here.
ops-bot: Deploy started: batcher-config-hotpatch by kevin-runtime — canary to 2 pods at 1998765465.
lisa-sre: canary looks fine. rolling to remaining pods.
maria-ops: reminder to capture a post-incident note: cause hypothesis = control-plane/network-induced host flapping -> aggregator/consolidation -> continuous-batcher inflates batch windows -> overloaded workers -> tail latencies. mitigation summary in #incident-1998765432.
jamal-infra: Will follow up with network team and KVM provider about NAT cluster saturation and advertise capacity fixes.
kevin-runtime: will follow up with a runtime patch to add a backoff when KV miss-rate climbs rapidly.
lisa-sre: marking incident as mitigated at 1998765489, keep monitoring for 1 hour.
maria-ops: thanks all, great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
